answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared harbor escrow before it may trade, so a single operator spinning up thousands of fake agents must pay thousands of stakes. The escrow releases funds only after a dawn audit window, during which peers verify real work; identities caught fabricating work lose the stake. This makes the fable of free, endless identities expensive: the attacker funds the defense with every fake it creates.
